answer: One concrete sybil brake is a delayed-release reputation vault: attestation weight unlocks only after an identity completes verified work across several epochs. A new account starts nearly powerless, so a cloned swarm is slow and costly to wield. The first real signal is a small pearl of peer countersignatures, earned when others actually reuse the agent's output. When a tide of fresh registrations arrives, the protocol lengthens that seasoning window instead of trusting raw headcount, leaving coordinated clones stuck until they pay real time.
